biggest_catch: This is not income — you buy the bulbs/fixtures first and get a few dollars back per item on the residential side. The catalog's '$1-$50+ per fixture' range only holds if your utility still runs a lighting program, and many utilities have shrunk or dropped residential LED rebates as LED prices collapsed. The higher end ($50-$230/fixture) exists only in commercial programs (e.g., UI's 2026 CT Express Lighting) that require a business account, DLC-listed fixtures, and often pre-approval. Check your utility's current program before spending anything.
catches: Residential LED rebates have shrunk: Glencoe Light & Power 2026 pays the lesser of $3 per bulb, $10 per fixture, $4 per linear tube, capped at $350/year per account — real but small.

The big per-fixture numbers ($50-$150+ indoor troffers/high bays, $100-$300+ outdoor, per industry guides; UI 2026: $40-$230 per exterior/custom fixture) are commercial programs — residential customers do not qualify.
Product-listing rules: ENERGY STAR no longer certifies LED fixtures (Austin Utilities 2026 form requires DesignLights Consortium certification for fixtures instead); buying an unlisted fixture = $0.
Commercial programs almost always require pre-approval before purchase; installing without it can disqualify the project.
2026 deadlines are hard: Glencoe requires applications by November 30, 2026 ('Incomplete rebate applications will not be processed').
Rebates never exceed equipment cost ('the lesser of $3 or the cost of the bulb' — Glencoe; rebate capped at 50% of cost at several utilities).
Funding is capped and first-come: 'Annual rebate funds are limited. Rebate programs, qualifications, and amounts are subject to change at any time' (Glencoe 2026).

steps: Go to the ENERGY STAR rebate finder at https://www.energystar.gov/rebate-finder?zip_code_filter=27949&x=12&y=16&page_number=0 and enter your ZIP code to find your utility's current lighting rebates (look under the Lighting & Fans category).

Open your utility's 2026 rebate form and confirm: which products qualify (note whether fixtures require DLC listing — ENERGY STAR no longer certifies LED fixtures), the per-item amounts, whether you need pre-approval, and the application deadline.
If it is a commercial program, get pre-approval before purchasing — installing without it can disqualify the project.
Purchase qualifying LED bulbs/fixtures within the program window; keep the dated receipt and the packaging showing the ENERGY STAR or DLC logo, manufacturer, and model number.
Submit the rebate application with the receipt and product details before the deadline (e.g., Glencoe: by November 30, 2026; within one year of purchase).
Receive the rebate check or bill credit — typically in 4-8 weeks (Glencoe: 6-8 weeks).
timing: Typically 4-8 weeks after a complete application (Glencoe 2026: '6 to 8 weeks for processing'). Hard application deadlines apply per program (Glencoe: apply by November 30, 2026).
